results.title: Monet’s Riviera, 90s nostalgia and Bayeux à gogo! The best art and architecture of autumn 2026 | Art and design | The Guardian
results.content:
Rendered in his signature emerald-absinthe tones, Toor’s paintings tell the imagined lives of young, queer south Asian men. Much like near-contemporary Lynette Yiadom-Boakye, he inserts fictionalised subjects into paintings in the traditions of the masters to tell enigmatic, evocative, and gently subversive stories. BECourtauld, London, 2 October to 10 January

## Wakaliga Uganda [...] Artists didn’t just paint the Riviera; they helped invent it. The rise of France’s Mediterranean coast as a holiday resort from the 1870s onwards coincided with the new, savage embrace of raw sunlight by Monet and Cézanne. Matisse and the Fauves painted the Riviera in psychedelic colours, but it was Picasso who saw beach life as erotic and shockingly modern. JJRoyal Academy, London, 2 October to 31 January

## Salman Toor: Someone Like You [...] Istanbul really was Constantinople once – the eastern capital of the Roman empire that survived as the centre of Byzantine civilisation. When the Ottomans conquered it in 1453 they respected this, preserving the ancient domed church Haghia Sophia and modelling mosques on it. This survey of art and design from one of the world’s most hypnotic cities, from Byzantine icons to Turkish tamburs, sounds stupendous. JJ V&A, London, 7 November to 9 May
